title: Water Depth from Time-of-Flight

Δt.description: Time difference between surface and bottom returns

c_w.description: Speed of light in water (≈ 0.225 m/ns; varies with temperature, salinity)

θ_w.description: Refracted beam angle in water (from Snell's law)

applicability: Accounts for oblique incidence — off-nadir beams travel longer path through water. For nadir beam: d = Δt × c_w / 2. Refraction index of water: n_w ≈ 1.333 (fresh) to 1.340 (seawater).

title: Snell's Law — Air-Water Refraction
applicability: The refracted beam is deflected toward vertical upon entering water. For a 20° incidence: θ_w = arcsin(sin(20°)/1.333) ≈ 14.9°. This bends the beam, causing apparent position of bottom points to be offset from true position — refraction correction is essential.

title: Maximum Penetration Depth
applicability: Kd measured from Secchi disk: Kd ≈ 1.7/Secchi_depth. Or from turbidity: Kd ≈ 0.1 + 0.03 × Turbidity(NTU) (approximate). Clear ocean: Kd ≈ 0.05 → d_max ≈ 50 m. Moderate river: Kd ≈ 0.5 → d_max ≈ 5 m.
source: Guenther et al. (2000), Pe'eri et al. (2011)

title: Beam Footprint on Bottom

D_bottom.description: Beam footprint diameter at the bottom

D_surface.description: Beam footprint diameter at water surface

applicability: Refraction reduces divergence in water by factor 1/n_w. Typical surface footprint: 1–3 m (airborne). Bottom footprint in 10 m water: 2–5 m. Limits horizontal resolution of bathymetric features — fine features (< footprint) cannot be resolved.

title: Beer-Lambert Law — Attenuation in Water

I(d).description: Return signal intensity from depth d

I₀.description: Incident signal intensity at water surface

d.description: Water depth (factor of 2 for two-way path)

applicability: Signal attenuates exponentially with depth. At d_max, return signal ≈ noise floor of the detector. Two-way path means effective attenuation is 2×Kd per meter depth. Bottom reflectance also affects return signal — dark bottoms further reduce returns.

title: Vertical Accuracy — Bathymetric LiDAR

σ_d.description: Depth measurement uncertainty (timing, speed of light)

applicability: Typical total vertical uncertainty: 0.15–0.30 m (95%) in calm, clear conditions. Degrades with depth, turbidity, and wave action. Topo points: 0.05–0.15 m vertical (same as standard ALS). Bathy accuracy meets IHO S-44 Order 1b in optimal conditions.
